premises: Grain boundaries are the primary fast-diffusion paths for Cr–Zr interdiffusion in Cr coatings on Zr alloys at high temperature.
A dense, columnar Cr coating microstructure has fewer grain boundaries than a conventional, random-grain PVD Cr coating.
Reducing grain-boundary area in the Cr coating will significantly limit Cr diffusion into the Zr substrate during transient high-temperature events.
The tailored columnar microstructure can be achieved by adjusting PVD parameters (bias, temperature, rate) and will be stable under thermal cycling.
The optimized coating will maintain corrosion protection under subcritical water at ~300°C.
